office_does: The three county commissioners are Stevens County's legislative body: they adopt the budget, set county policy and oversee courthouses, the jail and county roads. District 2 is nominated by district but elected county-wide.
race_blurb: Commissioner Mark Burrows, a retired Chewelah police chief seeking re-election, faces first-time candidate Jack Griffin Jr. of Valley, who states no party preference. Burrows won 77% in the district-only primary.

candidates.summary: Stevens County commissioner for 5.5 years by his count and a retired Chewelah police chief and Air Force veteran, running to finish current projects and resist state overregulation.
highlights: Stresses efficiency and accountability, and competitive pay to retain county staff [S1]
Promises to work with other counties and sheriffs against 'overregulation' and 'unconstitutional legislation from the State' [S1]
Cast the lone vote against the county's 2025 veterans relief fund policy, calling it rushed [S4]
Did not answer questions at the July candidate forum [S6]

experience.basis: Incumbent commissioner with a 30-year law-enforcement career, running to see current projects through.

spending.basis: Frames stewardship as efficiency and accountability in county operations, while backing competitive pay for staff retention.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate from Valley who returned home after 40 years in corporate, tech, union and healthcare work.
highlights: First run for public office; states no party preference [S1]
Says he has accomplished 'a great deal with limited resources' over his career [S1]
Did not answer questions at the July candidate forum [S3]

experience.basis: First-time candidate offering private-sector experience in place of the incumbent; no generational-change argument.
